schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE EMP (NAME INT, DEPT INT, EMP INT);
CREATE TABLE DEPT (DEPT INT, LOC INT, MGR INT);
q1: SELECT X.NAME AS XN FROM EMP AS X WHERE (X.EMP, X.DEPT) IN (SELECT Y.MGR, Y.DEPT FROM DEPT AS Y WHERE Y.LOC = 3)
q2: SELECT X.NAME AS XN FROM EMP AS X
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT X.NAME AS XN FROM EMP AS X WHERE (X.EMP, X.DEPT) IN (SELECT Y.MGR, Y.DEPT FROM DEPT AS Y WHERE Y.LOC = 3)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT X.NAME AS XN FROM EMP AS X
counterexample:
INSERT INTO EMP (NAME, DEPT, EMP) VALUES (1, 1, 100), (2, 2, 101), (3, 1, 102);
INSERT INTO DEPT (DEPT, LOC, MGR) VALUES (1, 3, 102), (2, 4, 101);
explanation: Q1 selects employees whose (EMP, DEPT) pair matches a (MGR, DEPT) pair from DEPT where LOC = 3. Q2 selects all employees. They are not equivalent because Q1 filters employees based on a subquery condition, while Q2 returns all employees.
counterexample_dsp: Create a scenario where not all employees are managers of departments located at LOC = 3. This will show Q1 returns fewer rows than Q2.
